proof_boundary: This hierarchy is not a proof of eventual sign, RH, or Lambda<=0. The cofinal equivalence composes published Suzuki results with the internally audited fixed-omega phase theorem and requires independent expert review.

rows.proof_boundary: Exact arithmetic identity only.
rows.statement: c_omega(n)=n^omega*sum_(d|n)mu(d)d^(-2omega)=n^omega*product_(p|n)(1-p^(-2omega))>0.

rows.proof_boundary: Definition of the first smoothing weight only.
rows.statement: Suzuki's explicit beta-integral weight g_(omega,1) is supported on (0,1] for every 0<omega<1/2.

rows.proof_boundary: Exact logarithmic smoothing recursion only.
rows.statement: g_(omega,k+1)(x)=integral_x^1 sqrt(y/x)*g_(omega,k)(y)dy/y.

rows.proof_boundary: Exact finite arithmetic sum only.
rows.statement: H_(omega,k)(x)=x^(-1/2)*sum_(n<=x)c_omega(n)*g_(omega,k)(n/x), with H=0 on 0<x<1.

rows.proof_boundary: Exact smoothing identity; it supplies no eventual sign.
rows.statement: H_(omega,k+1)(x)=integral_1^x H_(omega,k)(y)dy/y.

rows.proof_boundary: Published Mellin identity only; contour continuation may not cross uncancelled denominator zeros.
rows.statement: integral_1^infinity H_(omega,k)(x)x^(1/2-s)dx/x=[xi(s-omega)/xi(s+omega)]/(s-1/2)^k, initially for Re(s)>1+omega.

rows.proof_boundary: Exact normalization bridge only.
rows.statement: H_(omega,1)(x)=sqrt(x)*h_omega^<1>(x) in the canonical-system notation.

rows.proof_boundary: The eventual-sign antecedent is not proved.
rows.statement: If H_(omega,k) has one sign for all sufficiently large x, Landau's theorem and the absence of real xi zeros remove every uncancelled pole of xi(s-omega)/xi(s+omega) in Re(s)>1/2.

rows.proof_boundary: The xi-specific growth input is essential.
rows.statement: For the xi quotient, pole-freeness in Re(s)>1/2 plus Suzuki's high-strip estimate and Phragmen-Lindelof gives reduced meromorphic innerness.

rows.proof_boundary: One fixed omega can still hide off-line zeros by exact horizontal cancellation.
rows.statement: Eventual one-sign behavior of one H_(omega,k) implies D(omega), the fixed-omega all-time determinant property.

rows.proof_boundary: Internally audited composition of published Landau machinery with the corpus fixed-omega phase theorem; external review is required.
rows.statement: If omega_j decreases to zero and every H_(omega_j,k_j) is eventually one-signed for some integers k_j>=1, then RH.

rows.proof_boundary: Conditional asymptotic; it cannot be used to prove its own antecedent.
rows.statement: Under RH, H_(omega,1)(x)=1+O_omega(x^(-B_omega)) for some B_omega>0 and each fixed 0<omega<1/2.

rows.proof_boundary: Conditional contour shift only.
rows.statement: Under RH, H_(omega,k)(x) has positive leading term (log x)^(k-1)/(k-1)! for every fixed k>=2.

rows.proof_boundary: The forward implication uses Suzuki's RH-conditional asymptotics; the reverse implication is a corpus sharpening requiring external review.
rows.statement: RH is equivalent to the existence of omega_j decreasing to zero and integers k_j>=1 for which every H_(omega_j,k_j) has an eventual single sign.

rows.proof_boundary: Exact endpoint sign, not a summatory sign.
rows.statement: g_(omega,1)(x)~-a_omega*x^(omega-1) as x->0+, where a_omega>0 for 0<omega<1/2.

rows.proof_boundary: Derived recursively; it proves every smoothing weight remains negative near zero.
rows.statement: g_(omega,k)(x)~-a_omega*(1/2-omega)^(-(k-1))*x^(omega-1) as x->0+.

rows.proof_boundary: Exact endpoint sign only.
rows.statement: For every k>=1, g_(omega,k)(x) is positive near x=1 and vanishes there like a positive constant times (1-x)^(omega+k-1).

rows.proof_boundary: Coefficient positivity cannot prove any smoothing level termwise.
rows.statement: Every g_(omega,k) is signed: negative near zero and positive near one, despite c_omega(n)>0.

rows.proof_boundary: No finite x grid closes the Landau antecedent.
rows.statement: Finite positivity of H_(omega,k) cannot establish eventual sign on an unbounded half-line.

rows.proof_boundary: Cofinality in omega is indispensable.
rows.statement: Eventual sign at one fixed omega gives innerness only at that shift; exact horizontal zero cancellation prevents promotion to RH.

rows.proof_boundary: This is the surviving RH-strength arithmetic obligation.
rows.statement: Prove eventual one-sign behavior for H_(omega_j,k_j) along one explicit sequence omega_j->0, with any chosen k_j>=1, by direct arithmetic inequalities that do not assume a zero-free region.
